name: Choroid Plexus Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Central Nervous System Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of malignant epithelial tumor cells with papillary architecture arising from choroid plexus epithelium
MRI or CT showing intraventricular mass with heterogeneous enhancement and possible hydrocephalus
High mitotic index and evidence of necrosis on histology
Detection of TP53 mutations or chromosomal abnormalities associated with malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant choroid plexus tumor with papillary architecture and high mitotic activity, supported by imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic carcinoma and other intraventricular tumors

pathognomonic.symptomName: Signs of increased intracranial pressure due to obstructive hydrocephalus
searchTerms: signs of increased brain pressure from fluid buildup
headache and nausea from brain swelling
rapidly enlarging head size in infants

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting unrelated to gastrointestinal causes
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting not caused by stomach issues

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion
breathing problems from brain fluid buildup
abnormal breathing due to brain pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-diagnostic but may show elevated protein
Elevated intracranial pressure on lumbar puncture contraindicates procedure
imaging: MRI showing large, heterogeneously enhancing intraventricular mass
CT scan demonstrating hydrocephalus and calcifications within tumor
other: Histopathology revealing papillary structures with high mitotic activity and necrosis
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin and transthyretin

distinguishingFeatures: Benign histology with low mitotic index
Lack of necrosis and invasive growth
Arises from ependymal cells lining ventricles
Different histopathological features including perivascular pseudorosettes
Immunohistochemistry inconsistent with choroid plexus origin

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infants
Signs of acute hydrocephalus such as sudden vomiting and decreased consciousness
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System. 5th ed. IARC; 2021.
Rickert CH, Paulus W. Tumors of the choroid plexus. Microsc Res Tech. 2001;52(1):104-111.
Fisher PG, et al. Choroid plexus carcinoma: a review of clinical features and treatment. J Neurooncol. 2004;67(3):271-279.
